notes:
31 stations, lines 5195-5234. There are no sub-headings inside the list, so coast is the section heading, IRISH COAST.

How I recorded the fields:
- Fragments have the line's leading indentation removed. Spacing inside a line is kept exactly. Line 5213 is part of the South Rock row and holds two pieces on one printed line: the place ("Down,") and the second keeper, so it is one fragment with the printed gap between them.
- other gives the printed run of columns in order: SF, LW, remarks on schedules, Sp, Au, MS ("--" means no miles from shore given). The column padding is kept as printed.
- Numbers: the "." after each number is punctuation and is dropped. The asterisk is part of the number: 5* vs 5_a_, 8* vs 8, 14* vs 14. So marks is null for every row. No station is printed in italics; only the letters a and b in 5_a_, 7_a_ and 12_b_ are.
- Names and places: the comma between a name and its county is dropped. "Co." appears only for Fastnet. "do." (ditto) is kept as printed in place. Following the county above, it means Wexford (rows 6, 7, 7_a_), Wicklow (8*), Antrim (14), Donegal (17-22) and Galway (32, 34).
- Old Head is split as name "Old Head, Kinsale" with place "Cork" (the Old Head of Kinsale).
- "Maidens, South Antrim" is split as name "Maidens, South" with place "Antrim", because the next row has "Maidens, North do.". Maidens South is 14* and Maidens North is 14.
- Light-ship types are kept as printed: "LS" for most, but "Lt.-ship" for South Rock. No light characters are given in this list.
- Keepers joined by "and" are split into separate people. Full stops that only end the row are dropped.

Spellings and possible slips (kept as printed):
- "Arran Island, Is." is probably a misprint for N. (North). Compare "Arran Island, S." just below it.
- "Howth Baily" (Baily), "Innishtrahull", "Arranmore", "Broadhaven" and "Skelligs" are kept as printed.
- Row 34's remark ends "very good." with a full stop where most rows have a comma. Probably just typography.

Names that appear at two stations (could be transfers, or copying errors in the list):
- Richard Hamilton: Hook Tower and Maidens, North.
- Henry Kelly: Rockabill and Tory Island.
- Henry Williams and Thomas Fortune: both at Arranmore and at Arran Island, Is., in reversed order.
- Also P. Page (Tuskar) and Charles P. Page (Arran Island, S.), and Patrick Corish (Tuskar) and J. Corish (Maidens, South).

Checks against the totals printed with the list:
- The Sp and Au marks agree with the stated totals: 23 x for Spring and 28 x for Autumn.
- The LW column adds up to 141, but the note at line 5236 says 142 legs and wings were received. The extra one may be the Hoopoe sent by Eagle Island, East, which has no row in the list.

The note at lines 5236-5244 lists 11 stations left out (Galley Head, Dungarvan, Kish Light-ship, Copeland or Mew Island, Oyster Island N., Blacksod Point, Clare Island, Slyne Head N., Straw Island, Valentia, Dursey Island). It also names four new stations, all of which are in the list: Hook Tower, Lucifer Shoals, South Rock Light-ship and Maidens, North.
